reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that plate discipline is not a static aggregate but a dynamic decision-making process. Each pitch presents a binary choice—swing or take—with associated probabilistic outcomes. The xgboost model estimates these outcome probabilities conditioned on pitch location and hitter skill. Expected runs are calculated for each outcome, enabling computation of expected run differentials (ΔR) between swing and take. This ΔR becomes the primary metric for quantifying plate discipline. The model assumes rationality in decision-making and that run expectancy changes are predictable within a Markovian framework. Failure modes arise when the model underestimates variability in human behavior or when game situations are not adequately encoded into features. The method avoids simplistic metrics like O-Swing% by focusing on individual pitch-level decisions rather than season-long aggregations.
